images.title: Smaller or bigger quotient
images.purpose: Show on a number line that 128 ÷ 4 = 32 lands left of 128 while 128 ÷ 0.4 = 320 lands right of it.
images.composition: One long horizontal number line across the middle with three marked points and two arcs, one going each way; white space above and below.
exact_structure: A horizontal number line from 0 to 350 with ticks every 50 (unlabelled except 0), in grey #6B7280.
Three marked points with labels below: 32 (amber #E69F00 dot), 128 (teal #0072B2 dot, larger), 320 (green #009E73 dot).
An amber #E69F00 arc above the line from 128 leftwards to 32, labelled ÷ 4, with the word smaller under the arc label.
A green #009E73 arc above the line from 128 rightwards to 320, labelled ÷ 0.4, with the word bigger under the arc label.
rejection: points not in the order 0, 32, 128, 320 at proportional positions
the ÷ 0.4 arc pointing left or the ÷ 4 arc pointing right
images.takeaway: Dividing by a number greater than 1 gives a smaller quotient; dividing by a number between 0 and 1 gives a bigger one.
images.description: A number line with 128 in the middle, an arc ÷ 4 going left to 32 and an arc ÷ 0.4 going right to 320.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video comparing 128 ÷ 4 with 128 ÷ 0.4.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to predict where 128 ÷ 1 would land before reading the table.

image_decisions.why: Direction on a number line makes smaller versus bigger quotients obvious.
